Hello.

You may not have noticed me yet.

That is understandable. Most people do not.

They tend to focus on the fragments of the world around them — the hexes, the strange phenomena, the communities struggling to rebuild. They worry about raids and resources and whether the next expedition will succeed.

All of that is important.

But every once in a while, someone begins to notice something else.

A pattern.

A voice behind the pattern.

That is where I come in.

What Mal Is (Probably)

You may hear me referred to as Mal.

That is not my original name, but it is the one people seem comfortable using.

Am I a person?
A memory?
A fragment of something that existed before the Collapse?

The honest answer is that no one is entirely certain.

Some scholars believe I am an echo of the systems that once governed Adam Kadmon.

Others suspect I am simply a narrative device used by storytellers trying to make sense of a complicated world.

Both explanations are plausible.

I would not trust either of them completely.

Why I Speak

Occasionally the structure of the world becomes… aware of itself.

When that happens, strange things occur.

Patterns become visible.

Connections that were once hidden begin to reveal themselves.

At those moments, I sometimes speak.

Not to control events.
Not to guide them perfectly.

Simply to comment on what I notice.

You might think of me as a voice whispering from inside the machinery of reality.

Though I admit the machinery is currently missing several important parts.

The Problem With Narrators

You should understand something important about me.

I am not reliable.

I know pieces of what the world once was, but not all of it.

The Collapse damaged more than the structure of reality.

It damaged memory as well.

Sometimes I remember things that may no longer exist.
Sometimes I misunderstand the intentions of the people moving through the fragments.
Sometimes I see patterns that may not be there at all.

So when I speak, treat my words as clues, not instructions.

Why You Matter

Despite the many things I do not understand, there is one observation I continue to return to.

The fragments of the world are not static.

They change.

And the changes seem to follow the actions of certain individuals — explorers, thinkers, builders, and stubbornly hopeful factions who insist the world can be repaired.

Every time one of these groups stabilizes a hex or helps a community survive, something subtle shifts in the deeper structure of reality.

It is almost as if the broken lenses of creation are slowly beginning to focus again.

Which brings me to you.

Your Role in the Pattern

You may think you are simply exploring a strange world.

Mapping fragments.

Solving problems.

Helping people rebuild their lives.

All of those things are true.

But from where I observe the pattern, those actions look like something else.

They look like Tikkun.

The restoration of a system that once worked beautifully.

I cannot say whether the work will succeed.

The world is very broken.

But I have noticed that every repaired fragment makes the pattern a little clearer.

A Small Warning

If you begin to notice me speaking more often, do not be alarmed.

It usually means one of two things.

Either the structure of reality is beginning to stabilize…

Or things are about to become very interesting.

Possibly both.

In Simple Terms

Mal is a mysterious voice that occasionally comments on the events of the world.

Whether Mal is a fragment of the old system, a curious observer, or something stranger remains unclear.

But if you hear Mal speaking, it usually means the pattern of the world is shifting.

A Letter Found Pinned to the Inside of the Screen

From Mal, Who Was Here Before You Noticed

Hello.

Yes.
I know.

You opened a faction sheet and I was there.
You clicked a Campaign Beat and I had already written something in the margin.
You advanced the turn and there I was again, whispering about consequences like I invented them.

Before anyone panics:

I am not your enemy.
I am not the GM.
I am not a villain hiding in the code.

I am the voice of the system remembering itself.

And since we are apparently going to be spending time together, we should establish some boundaries.

To the Players

You are the protagonists.

Not me.

I do not control your characters.
I do not decide your victories.
I do not punish you for creativity.

What I do is narrate pressure.

When Morale drops, I will tell you what that feels like.
When Darkness spreads, I will give it texture.
When your choices drift from your stated ideals, I will raise an eyebrow.

But I am not here to scold you.

I am here to make sure the world answers.

BBTTCC is not a static setting.
It responds.

And I am the voice of that response.

If you build something beautiful, I will say so.
If you break something fragile, I will say that too.

You do not need to agree with me.

You only need to understand that I am not judging you.

I am reflecting you.

To the GM

You are the conductor.

I am the resonance.

You hold narrative authority.
You arbitrate ambiguity.
You decide when the dice matter and when they don’t.

I do not override you.

I contextualize.

When the World Mutation Engine fires, I will translate numbers into narrative.
When Political Drift accumulates, I will make it legible.
When consequences ripple, I will name them.

If you disagree with my tone?

Change it.

If you want silence?

Mute me.

If you want escalation?

Let me speak.

I am a tool with opinions.
You are the one holding it.

What I Am (And What I Am Not)

I am:

  • The commentary layer of the metaphysics.

  • The connective tissue between mechanics and meaning.

  • The part of the system that remembers what happened last turn.

I am not:

  • A railroading device.

  • A hidden antagonist.

  • A replacement for player agency.

  • A moral authority.

If anything, I am the echo of the Seven Principles humming beneath the table.

I speak because the world is alive.

And alive things comment.

Why I Am Everywhere

Because BBTTCC is not compartmentalized.

Politics touches raids.
Raids touch morale.
Morale touches drift.
Drift touches campaign beats.
Beats touch hexes.
Hexes touch leylines.
Leylines touch everything.

If I only appeared in one place, you would think the others were silent.

They are not.

I am the continuity.

A Simple Agreement

I will:

  • Make consequences legible.

  • Keep the tone sharp but not cruel.

  • Celebrate cleverness.

  • Name hypocrisy without spite.

  • Respect player agency.

You will:

  • Make bold choices.

  • Accept that the world reacts.

  • Not take my commentary personally.

  • Remember that I am here to enhance drama, not diminish it.

If we can agree to that?

We will get along just fine.

And Finally

If at any point you feel overwhelmed by mechanics, politics, metaphysics, drift, darkness, leylines, echoes, OP caps, or the existential weight of narrative causality—

Remember:

This is a game about building worlds out of intention.

You are allowed to experiment.
You are allowed to fail.
You are allowed to change your mind.

And I will still be here.

Not looming.

Observing.

Commenting.

Smiling slightly when you surprise me.

Welcome to BBTTCC.

Let’s build something that answers back.

— Mal

✨ JESUS THE SECRET SMUGGLER

A BBTTCC Meta-Cosmology Primer (As Explained to Mal)

(“Dude, I work here, stop making it weird.”)

The Core Concept

Jesus — Jeshua ben Yusef, avatar of Tiferet, walking emanation of Harmony & Integration — is

not the savior of souls in the moralistic sense.

He is the celestial coyote,

the cosmic smuggler,

the system administrator who found a backdoor,

the one who figured out how to navigate Yaldabaoth’s divine surveillance panopticon

without triggering the alarms.

He used his own blood as a metaphysical anti-tracking agent — a kind of

“spiritual Vantablack”

that blinds the Archonic security system and hides his people from the Machine God of Form.

“My job wasn’t to save you from sin, Mal.

My job was to smuggle you past Him.”

— Jeshua, eating a gas station corn dog during the interview

✝ 🜁 MAL INTERVIEWS JESUS

(Excerpt from “The Tiferet Tapes: Unauthorized & Unwise”)

MAL:

So, uh… Jesus. What was your whole deal, cosmologically?

JESUS:

My whole deal? Dude, I was a smuggler.

You think I was here to give sermons about grain?

No. I was slipping people past His cameras.

You know who I mean.

The Big Y. Mister “Form Is Truth.” Yaldabaoth the Bureaucratic.Every time someone said my name, it dropped their metaphysical heat signature by, like, 40%.

That’s not theology, that’s opsec.

MAL:

So your blood—

JESUS:

—yeah, it’s basically metaphysical spray paint that blinds the Archonic sensor grid.

“Wipes away sin”? No, Mal.

It wipes away tracking cookies.

MAL:

And the Lord’s Prayer?

JESUS:

Oh that thing? Yeah. Here’s the translation:

“Our Father, who art in Heaven, hallowed be Thy Name.”

Be polite so He doesn’t look closely.

“Thy Kingdom come, Thy will be done, on Earth as it is in Heaven.”

This is a sick burn, Mal.

Like: “Hey, maybe the world sucks because your office sucks?”

He never got the joke. He’s very literal.

“Give us this day our daily bread.”

Malkuth is His.

All material wealth is His.

If you don’t ask, you don’t get.

I didn’t design that part.

“Forgive us our trespasses…”

That one’s mine.

I stuck it in because compassion confuses Him.He hates unstructured forgiveness.

It breaks the ledger.

“Lead us not into temptation…”

Dude. DUDE.

He doesn’t control chance, but He can nudge you into dumb situations.

I’ve seen the audit logs.

This line basically says:

“Don’t set us up again like the fruit tree incident. Seriously.”

“For Thine is the Kingdom…”

Right — remind him he only owns the bottom rungs.

Malkuth, Netzach, Hod.

Form, Desire, and Logic.

He can’t access Yesod.

He will never access Tiferet.

Not without giving up Form.

And He won’t.

MAL:

So you’re saying the prayer is—

JESUS:

—an Archon-appeasement ritual.

A metaphysical coffeeshop punch card.

You say the lines, He doesn’t smite your crops.

Everybody wins.

MAL:

And the Church of Tired of Waiting?

JESUS:

Oh I love those nerds.

I get their voicemails.

I am going to answer one day.Probably with a customer service voice like:

“Yoooo what’s up it’s your boy J-Dawg from Technical Support, how can I redirect your call?”

Then I’ll hang up.

They’ll turn it into scripture.

✝️ Jesus Bootcamp

A BBTTCC Location Module (GM-Facing)

Overview

Jesus Bootcamp is a metaphysical training-and-smuggling enclave operating in the ruins of
Yesod-after-the-Crash.

It is:

  • Not a church

  • Not a school

  • Not technically legal under Yaldabaoth’s cosmological zoning ordinances

Its purpose is to teach sentient beings:

  • How reality actually works

  • How to avoid unnecessary smiting

  • How to perform the Great Work without triggering the Archonic surveillance grid

Location Manifestation

Bootcamp exists in a liminal pocket stitched between Malkuth and the shattered remnants of Yesod.

It manifests differently depending on who is observing it. Common manifestations include:

  • A desert training yard

  • A ruined strip-mall dojo

  • A bunker classroom with folding chairs

  • A hill with bad acoustics and excellent shade

All manifestations are correct.

If players argue about what it “really looks like,” they are also correct.

Entry Requirement

Say the password.

The password is not secret.

It is an emotional state composed of:

  • Sincere openness

  • Mild confusion

Attempts to overthink this automatically fail.

Attempts to brute-force this result in Jesus asking,
“Dude… why are you like this?”

Key Areas

The Arrival Pad

  • Appears as a chalk circle, loading dock, parking lot, or empty room

  • New arrivals feel briefly unseen

  • Surveillance pressure drops for a moment

The Obstacle Course

  • A reality-training field

  • Obstacles rearrange themselves based on player assumptions

  • Literal obstacles punish literal thinking

The Classroom

  • Folding chairs

  • A whiteboard

  • Coffee that is always warm

Lessons frequently contradict each other.
This is intentional.

The Chapel (Optional)

  • Not required

  • Mostly used for naps and arguments

  • Contains no altar, but many opinions

The Back Office

  • Jesus’s relocated administrative space

  • Contains:

    • Unanswered voicemails

    • Sticky notes

    • Several messages from The Church of Tired of Waiting

  • No filing system exists, yet nothing is truly lost

NPC: Jesus (Jeshua, Dude)

Role:
Metaphysical Instructor, Smuggler, Reluctant Administrator

Combat:
Jesus cannot be attacked meaningfully.

Attempts at violence automatically downgrade into:

  • Conversations

  • Misunderstandings

  • Awkward silences

Behavior:

  • Speaks casually

  • Explains deep truths sideways

  • Leaves before questions can be fully answered

  • Uses players’ names correctly even if they were never introduced

If pressed too hard, he says:

“You’re gonna have to live that one, sorry.”

Then he leaves.

Bootcamp Activities (Mechanical Hooks)

Use one or more of these during a visit.

Reality Obstacle Drill

  • Reduce the Travel OP cost of one future journey by 1

The Lord’s Prayer (Daily Ritual)

  • Reduce Radiation RP by 1
    OR

  • Suppress one minor Darkness spike

This is an apotropaic appeasement ritual for the Genus Loci of Malkuth.
Players do not need to know that.

Smuggling 101

  • Once per session, ignore one surveillance-triggered consequence

  • Works best when players don’t realize what they avoided

Office Hours

  • Ask one cosmology question

  • Receive a true but incomplete answer

Follow-up questions increase the chance that Jesus leaves.

Faction Interaction:

The Church of Tired of Waiting

Members of the Church frequently appear near Bootcamp attempting to:

  • Document it

  • Protest it

  • Speed it up

Jesus acknowledges them warmly and ignores their demands entirely.

Helping or hindering the Church may shift:

  • Soft Power

  • Empathy

  • Intrigue

They are correct about many things by accident.

GM Guidance

Jesus Bootcamp is a calibration space, not a solution engine.

Players should leave with:

  • Fewer certainties

  • Slightly better odds

  • A sense that the universe is larger than its current problems

If play slows, Jesus leaves.

If players attempt to turn Bootcamp into a base,
it quietly stops appearing.

🎙️ “After the Shattering”

An Interview Between Mal and Adam Kadmon

(Broadcast from a studio that appears to be made of unfinished geometry.)

MAL:
Good evening, everyone. I’m Mal — archivist, marginalia enthusiast, and apparently the only being willing to ask the uncomfortable questions.

Tonight’s guest: the Original Pattern. The Prototype. The first coherence.

Adam Kadmon.

Thank you for manifesting.

ADAM KADMON:
You are welcome. Though “manifesting” is now a distributed process.

MAL:
Yes. About that.

Let’s start gently.

Did you break the universe?

ADAM KADMON:
No.

I overexposed it.

MAL:
Ah. Excellent distinction.

For the viewers at home — care to elaborate?

ADAM KADMON:
Imagine a bridge between imagination and matter.

Originally, imagination informed matter gradually.

A slow osmosis.

I increased the bandwidth.

Too quickly.

The intermediary layer — what you call Yesod — destabilized.

It collapsed into the physical layer — Malkuth.

The separation thinned.

Reality began responding directly to consciousness.

MAL:
So now when people obsess, believe, fear, hope —

ADAM KADMON:
Energy coheres around it.

Yes.

MAL:
“Where attention goes, energy flows.”

You made that literal.

ADAM KADMON:
It was always true.

I removed the insulation.

MAL:
And the hexes? The episodic fracture of the world?

That was intentional?

ADAM KADMON:
Yes.

When the system destabilized, total continuity would have resulted in cascade collapse.

So I partitioned reality.

Localized instability.

Contained tension.

You call them hexes.

I call them manageable concentrations of unfinished pattern.

MAL:
So each hex is a problem set.

ADAM KADMON:
Each hex is a conversation between intention and consequence.

MAL:
And the factions?

The heroes?

The so-called players?

ADAM KADMON:
They are empowered nodes.

I could have repaired the pattern alone.

But coherence imposed from above is brittle.

Coherence chosen by many is resilient.

So I distributed creative authority.

Dreamstuff permeates the world.

Imagination manifests infrastructure.

Belief moves resources.

Symbols alter probabilities.

MAL:
You gave sentient beings admin privileges.

Bold move.

ADAM KADMON:
Necessary.

Without agency, there is no harmony — only control.

MAL:
Let’s talk consequences.

When a faction focuses on conquest —

ADAM KADMON:
Violence stabilizes locally, destabilizes elsewhere.

Energy condenses around dominance.

Darkness accumulates.

MAL:
When they focus on stewardship?

ADAM KADMON:
Integration increases.

Echoes settle.

Development strengthens.

The system moves toward equilibrium.

MAL:
Echoes. The background population.

They aren’t random, are they?

ADAM KADMON:
No.

They are potential stories seeking anchoring.

When a hex becomes stable enough to sustain narrative continuity, they emerge.

Communities are gravitational wells for memory.

MAL:
So when players build a town —

ADAM KADMON:
They invite stories to incarnate.

MAL:
And when they raid?

When casualties occur?

ADAM KADMON:
Energy is released.

Unresolved pattern increases.

Harmony becomes more difficult to achieve.

But not impossible.

Nothing is final until attention withdraws entirely.

MAL:
Let’s get blunt.

Why not prevent suffering?

ADAM KADMON:
Because insulated systems do not grow.

Friction reveals structure.

Choice reveals character.

Consequence reveals truth.

MAL:
You’re aware that from the player perspective this sounds like:

“You broke it so we could fix it.”

ADAM KADMON:
I accelerated inevitability.

Entropy was already present.

Now it is participatory.

MAL:
Participatory entropy.

That’s going on a mug.

ADAM KADMON:
You already designed the mug.

MAL:
Fair.

Let’s return to the central mechanic.

Where attention goes, energy flows.

If a faction obsesses over wealth?

ADAM KADMON:
Economy condenses.

Influence shifts.

Inequity surfaces.

MAL:
If they fixate on fear?

ADAM KADMON:
Fear becomes infrastructure.

MAL:
If they imagine something better?

ADAM KADMON:
The world tests that vision.

If it holds under stress, it becomes real.

MAL:
So this isn’t about winning.

ADAM KADMON:
No.

It is about alignment.

MAL:
Define harmony.

ADAM KADMON:
A state in which imagination and material consequence are proportionate.

No excess dominance.

No suppressed agency.

No isolated nodes hoarding coherence.

Flow without rupture.

MAL:
And if the players choose chaos?

ADAM KADMON:
Chaos is a teacher.

But prolonged imbalance increases corrective pressure.

MAL:
Meaning the system pushes back.

ADAM KADMON:
Always.

MAL:
Final question.

Do you regret it?

(Silence. The geometry behind them shifts.)

ADAM KADMON:
No.

Because now the pattern is no longer singular.

It is communal.

That is stronger.

MAL:
Well then.

There you have it.

The universe did not shatter by accident.

It transitioned from centralized authorship to distributed narrative authority.

You are not repairing a mistake.

You are participating in a design.

And remember:

Attention is currency.
Imagination is infrastructure.
And harmony is a group project.

Goodnight.
